title: Half Full Without a Scale
surface: A transparent bottle is narrow at the top and wide below, with no volume scale. Without pouring, weighing or measuring it, a woman marks the water level, seals the bottle and turns it upside down. After the water settles, one look proves it is exactly half full. What does she see?
solution: The settled water surface meets the same marked cross-section of the bottle. Upright, water occupies one side of that section; inverted, it occupies the other. The water volume has not changed, so the two regions have equal capacity. An irregular bottle shape does not matter.

facts.text: Both settled water surfaces correspond to the same marked cross-section of the bottle.
The same volume fills opposite sides after inversion, proving each is half the bottle’s capacity.
The sealed bottle neither leaks nor changes shape.

unknowns: Its material, capacity and exact dimensions are unspecified.
hints: What becomes of the region originally occupied by air?
Compare the water surfaces against the same physical mark.
Equal volumes occupy opposite sides of the marked cross-section.
